answer.exemplar: The area of a region bounded by a polar curve is the accumulation of very thin triangles, each with its vertex at the pole and its two other vertices on the curve close together. If the radius there is r and the angle swept is a small amount d theta, the third side of that triangle is nearly r d theta, so the triangle has area one half times r times r d theta, that is one half r squared d theta, exactly as any triangle with two sides r enclosing an angle d theta does. Adding up all of these thin triangles from the start angle to the end angle gives one half of the integral of r squared with respect to theta, so the half is built into the geometry of the wedges rather than inserted afterwards to fix a factor. Two checks confirm it. For a constant radius r over a full turn the formula gives one half of r squared times 2pi, which is pi r squared, the familiar area of a circle. And for a sector of angle d theta of that same circle the formula gives one half of r squared times d theta, which is the standard sector area of one half r squared theta. A student who integrates r squared alone gets four times the correct area, which is the area of the circumscribed square rather than the circle, and the factor of two in each direction is exactly what the triangles account for.

questions.explanation: The factor of one half is not a correction, it is a piece of ordinary geometry carried into integral form. Two radii of lengths r1 and r2 separated by a small angle d theta enclose a triangle whose area is one half r1 r2 sine of d theta, and as the angle shrinks that becomes one half r squared d theta for a curve of radius r. So the area of a whole region is the accumulation of these thin triangles, which is exactly one half of the integral of r squared. The same half appears in the ordinary area formula pi r squared, since integrating a constant radius over a full turn gives one half of r squared times 2pi, which is pi r squared.
questions.hint: Compare with the formula for the area of a triangle in terms of two sides and the angle between them.
